Subject: Questions on retention and erasure language in DPA draft

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed and we have a few specific questions around the retention / erasure language and cross-border handling before we can proceed with commercial review:

1) Backups & replicas: The current clause says "Redwood will delete Customer Data from its active systems and backups in accordance with the Erasure Window." Can you confirm whether "backups" includes disaster recovery snapshots and cold storage? Globex needs an auditable guarantee that no customer data remains in any copies beyond the agreed erasure window unless a legal hold is in place.

2) Legal hold vs scheduled erasure: We need a clear mechanism where a legal hold overrides scheduled erasure and an audit trail is produced (who issued the hold, timestamp, scope, and release).

3) Cross-border movement: Does Redwood allow automatic cross-border replication (US <-> EU)? If so, what controls exist to pin data to EU-only processing for regulated data? We want explicit language for regional residency or an onshore processing addendum.

4) BYOK and key separation: Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-held keys for encryption-at-rest (BYOK) and whether keys are stored in the EU region for EU residency commitments?

5) Evidence and certifications: What evidence can Redwood provide (logs, certificate of erasure, wipe audit) when erasure is requested? Is there an established SLA for providing that evidence?

Attached: DPA_draft_v3.docx (our annotated copy)

We'd prefer to get a written proposed clause for the erasure/backups flow that we can drop into the DPA. Can your team provide a proposed exhibit or redline? If it's easier, we can set up a 30-min call with legal and engineering.

Thanks,

Hi Lara,

Appreciate the detailed review — good questions. Looping in Marissa (Account) and Karthik (Product/Legal liaison) so we can pull together concrete language and technical details. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with proposed exhibit text by EOD Wed and can do a short call if helpful.

1) Backups & replicas: Our intended position is that "backups" includes both hot/cold snapshots and DR replicas. Practically, we differentiate: active storage truncation (erasure from live indexes) occurs within the Erasure Window (proposed 30 days), tombstones and metadata markers are retained to prevent resurrection for an additional period (60 days), and immutable backup tiers are scheduled for sanitization within 90 days. That said, we can tighten these windows for regulated customers in the EU to 30 days across active and backup copies for an addendum.

2) Legal hold: We support a documented Legal Hold mechanism. Holds are applied via our control plane, require formal request (signed JML / legal request), and create an append-only hold record with issuer, timestamp, scope, and reason. Holds suspend erasure and are flagged in our audit log; release requires an explicit release message. We'll provide sample audit entries and SLA for producing those logs (typically 3 business days).

3) Cross-border replication: By default, some features (replication, autoscaling) may route to nearest region to ensure latency; however, customers may opt into regional-only processing. For EU-only residency we offer a Private deployment or Dedicated capacity pinned to EU regions, and a DPA exhibit can require all processing to be in the EU.

4) BYOK: We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS integration). Keys can be provisioned in the EU under customer control for EU residency commitments. We'll include an operational note about key rotation and access logs in the exhibit.

5) Evidence & certifications: We can provide: (a) wipe certificate (signed by Redwood ops), (b) audit log extracts showing erasure events, and (c) SOC2 report references. We typically provide evidence within 5 business days (can be tightened).

Next steps: Karthik will draft proposed exhibit language (backup wipe timing, legal hold flow, BYOK statement, and audit SLA). Marissa will follow up on commercial implications for EU-only pining (estimated surcharge).

Hi Lara — attaching updated exhibit text below (also attached as proposed-dpa-exhibit-erase-clause.txt). This is intended as a starting point for redline and we kept the language narrow and operational. Happy to iterate.

--- BEGIN PROPOSED EXHIBIT TEXT ---
Erasure and Backup Handling Exhibit (Redwood Inference)

1. Definitions
  a. "Erasure Request": a Customer-authorized request to remove Customer Data from Redwood systems.
  b. "Erasure Window": the period within which Redwood will remove Customer Data from live/active systems ("Active Storage") and all backup and replica copies, unless a documented Legal Hold is in effect.

2. Erasure commitments for EU-Resident Data
  a. For Data subject to EU residency requirements ("EU-Resident Data"), Redwood shall remove Customer-identifiable data from Active Storage within 30 calendar days after receipt of a valid Erasure Request.
  b. Redwood shall sanitize backup and replication tiers such that no customer-identifiable data remains in any backup, replication, or cold storage tier more than 30 calendar days after the Erasure Request, except to the extent preserved under a documented Legal Hold.

3. Legal Hold
  a. A Legal Hold must be requested by Customer legal or authorized representative. Upon receipt, Redwood shall: (i) acknowledge receipt within 24 hours; (ii) create a persistent, append-only hold record containing issuer identity, timestamp, scope, and reason; and (iii) suspend any erasure actions for the scoped data.
  b. Redwood shall provide an audit extract of the hold record and impacted data sets within 3 business days of request. Release of a Legal Hold requires an explicit documented release by Customer.

4. BYOK and Key Residency
  a. Customer may provision and manage encryption keys (BYOK) via Redwood-supported KMS integrations. For EU-Resident Data, keys shall be stored and managed in an EU region under customer control; Redwood personnel shall not have access to plaintext without a documented legal process.

5. Evidence and Wipe Certificate
  a. Upon completion of Erasure, Redwood shall provide a Wipe Certificate signed by Redwood operations identifying the scope, timestamp, and method of erasure, along with redacted audit log entries showing the erasure events. Redwood shall deliver such evidence within 5 business days, or within 3 business days upon mutual agreement in the DPA.

6. Exceptions and Escrow
  a. The Parties may agree an exception where immutable archival copies require longer preservation for regulatory reasons; such exceptions must be documented in a signed exhibit and include an explicit end date for retention.

--- END PROPOSED EXHIBIT TEXT ---
